overview: TDEC's Division of Air Pollution Control requires a construction permit before building or modifying an air contaminant source unless it is exempt (Rule 1200-03-09), followed by an operating permit: true minor, conditional major (limits to stay below Title V), or Title V. Combined construction/operating permits are available. General permits (via Notice of Intent and Notice of Coverage) and Permits by Rule (via NOI and Notice of Authorization, Rule 1200-03-09-.07) cover listed categories. Major sources need PSD (BACT) in attainment areas or nonattainment NSR (LAER). Four local programs (Chattanooga-Hamilton, Knox, Memphis-Shelby, Nashville-Davidson) permit in their areas. Non-confidential submittals can be emailed to Air.Pollution.Control@tn.gov.

permitTypes.name: Exempt and insignificant activities
permitTypes.description: Exemptions are in Rule 1200-03-09-.04; farming equipment and mobile sources are exempt. Exempt and insignificant units must be designated in writing and listed in the Title V permit if the source is major. For PBR-listed federal-rule sources, insignificant status uses uncontrolled PTE thresholds.
permitTypes.thresholds: Insignificant status (PBR-listed federal rule sources): uncontrolled PTE below 5 TPY per criteria pollutant and below 1,000 lbs/yr per HAP (restated from TDEC's August 2025 permitting workshop).

permitTypes.name: Permit by Rule (PBR)
permitTypes.description: For minor sources in specific categories: gasoline dispensing facilities, stationary emergency internal combustion engines, and auto body refinishing (some excluded by Rule 1200-03-18). Obtained through a Notice of Intent and Notice of Authorization. Implemented starting 2017.

permitTypes.name: General Permits
permitTypes.description: G00001 perchloroethylene dry cleaners and G00002 petroleum solvent dry cleaners (expire February 1, 2027); G00003 concrete batch plants (expires March 11, 2034); G00004 nonmetallic mineral crushing and sizing (expires April 17, 2034); G00005 large concrete batch plants (expires May 15, 2035). Obtained through a Notice of Intent and Notice of Coverage. Construction application fees and annual fees apply to most general permit sources since 2024.
permitTypes.thresholds: G00003: concrete batch plants with emissions under 10 tons/year (restated from TDEC).

permitTypes.name: Construction Permit (minor NSR)
permitTypes.description: Required before building or modifying an air contaminant source unless exempt. Minor (non-Title V) applications should be submitted at least 90 days before construction; the Division has 115 days to issue after a complete application.

permitTypes.name: Non-Title V Operating Permit (true minor or conditional major)
permitTypes.description: Non-Title V construction permit holders apply within 30 days of startup. Conditional major permits take limits to stay below Title V thresholds. Typically issued for 10 years.

permitTypes.name: Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD)
permitTypes.description: Major NSR in attainment areas; requires BACT. Major/Title V and major NSR applications should be submitted at least 120 days before construction; the Division has 180 days to issue after a complete application.
permitTypes.thresholds: 100 TPY for listed industrial categories or 250 TPY for all other categories (restated from TDEC's August 2025 workshop).

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment NSR
permitTypes.description: Major NSR in nonattainment areas; requires LAER.
permitTypes.thresholds: Generally 100 TPY of the nonattainment pollutant or its designated precursors (restated).

permitTypes.name: Title V Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: Major sources, Title IV acid rain sources, and facilities required by federal rule (e.g., some landfills); lower thresholds apply in nonattainment areas. New applications are due within the construction permit's timeframe and no later than 360 days after startup; renewals 6 to 9 months before expiration; 5-year term. Draft permits get 30 days of public review and 45 days of EPA review.
permitTypes.thresholds: 10 tpy of any HAP, 25 tpy of combined HAPs, or 100 tpy of any regulated air pollutant (restated from TDEC's Air Permits page).

oilAndGas.summary: TDEC's air permit pages list no oil and gas specific general permit or PBR. Oil and gas sources follow the construction and operating permit requirements above and applicable federal NSPS/NESHAP.
